page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EDSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical Intel Xeon 8370C cores with hyper-threading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 2.8 GHz. The processor architecture is x86_64, supported by 48 KB L1d, 1 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache. It includes hardware flags such as AVX, AVX-512, and cryptography extensions like AES and SHA_NI, though it lacks AMX capabilities.

The instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a 614 GB SSD and supports Premium Storage. No GPUs are included in this configuration, and it does not provide complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark results place the E16ds_v5 in the average tier for most compute and memory operations. It achieves a Geekbench single-core score of 1642.0 and a multi-core score of 10078.0. Memory bandwidth tests show 837.18 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 52.98 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. In database and key-value store simulations, the server handles 15.92 million Redis SET operations per second and scores 7992.24 on PassMark database operations. Notably, it demonstrates strong performance in text generation for small LLM models, reaching 289.27 tokens per second, though medium model text generation drops to an average of 12.36 tokens per second.

With its high memory density and bundled local SSD storage, the E16ds_v5 offers a balanced cost-to-resource profile for memory-intensive workloads without requiring separate storage attachments. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent performance, making it suitable for relational databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and moderate-scale text processing or small-model language inference tasks.

It features 16 dedicated vCPUs (8 physical cores with hyper-threading), 128.0 GB of RAM, and a bundled 614 GB local SSD. Operating under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance delivers average performance across standard compute and memory benchmarks, including a Geekbench multi-core score of 10078.0 and a PassMark database score of 7992.24. It exhibits strong performance in text generation for small language models, achieving 289.27 tokens per second. Lacking GPU acceleration, the E16ds_v5 is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy workloads that benefit from local high-speed storage. It is suited for database hosting, caching layers, software compilation, and text processing workloads.
